label: Real run on this Mac's Docker Compose stack, with synthetic traffic from klaxon.traffic: synthetic data, a simulated provider, no real money. One fault from klaxon.faults, duplicate-delivery, was injected on purpose. The alert was raised by klaxon.alerts from what the stack showed. Klaxon's loop ran live on it, through Claude Code on Aravind's seat, and stopped on diagnosed after 7 steps; any reply it got is a recorded response, not a simulation. It was offered one write action (rollback_deploy), as in week 4; in an evaluation run its gate only plans an action the diagnosis names: nobody is asked, and nothing runs. The diagnosis was compared with the fault's recorded cause by a rule (klaxon.grading), not by a person or a model. Code planned the action its diagnosis named (redeploy ledger-consumer: LEDGER_HANDLER naive -> idempotent, LEDGER_BAD_EVENTS dead_letter (unchanged)); in an evaluation run nobody is asked, and nothing ran. The fault's cause was removed by the harness's clearing (klaxon.faults).

diagnosis.hypothesis: ledger-consumer was redeployed at 16:13:39Z with LEDGER_HANDLER=naive. That handler books every Kafka message and does not deduplicate by provider event_id. The provider resends each webhook until it is acknowledged, and webhook-receiver queues every resend as a new message (normal at-least-once delivery). Each copy was booked as its own ledger transaction: evt_000308 was posted 3 times and evt_000251 twice, seconds after the deploy. Each double posting is balanced, so ledger_balanced passes. provider_clearing grows by every duplicated amount, so the ledger runs $493.23 ahead and posted_exactly_once fails. The duplicated refund evt_000288 shows the other side. Open: the setting before the deploy is not visible, nor is the reason the provider resent these webhooks. I did not check every duplicate's timestamps.

evidence.shows: The money check confirms the alert. 7 events were posted 2-3 times and the ledger is +$493.23 against the provider. The ledger is balanced, and payments and refunds match the provider, so the fault is limited to ledger posting.
ledger-consumer was redeployed at 16:13:39Z with LEDGER_HANDLER=naive. It is the newest change, 17s before the alert; the other services were deployed at 16:12:12-13.
webhook-receiver queued evt_000308 three times (partition 0, offsets 98, 99 and 101, at 16:13:53-54Z). ledger-consumer posted each copy ($131.93 x3).
evt_000251 was queued twice (partition 2, offsets 73 and 76) and posted twice at 16:13:40Z, one second after the ledger-consumer deploy.
ledger-consumer logs only 'posted' lines and never a duplicate or skip message, so no already-booked check is running.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll ledger-consumer back to its settings from before the 16:13:39 deploy, expected to be an idempotent handler that dedups on event_id, to stop new duplicate postings. Then repair the ledger by reversing the extra transactions of the 7 duplicated events, keeping the first posting of each (for example, reverse 255 for evt_000251 and 265 for evt_000261). Rerun the money check afterwards.

diagnosis.blast_radius: ledger-consumer pauses while its container is recreated, so ledger posting is delayed. Events wait in Kafka for its consumer group, so nothing is lost. The rollback does not fix the duplicates already booked; they need a separate data repair. If the previous setting was also non-idempotent, duplicates would continue.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: Redeploy ledger-consumer with its current settings (LEDGER_HANDLER=naive, BAD_EVENTS=dead_letter), or roll forward to a known idempotent handler. Then rerun the money check.
